subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: The Void in Mythology
description: One-minute skill: The Void in Mythology.

hook.text: In the beginning, there was nothing. Genesis, Norse myth, and Greek cosmology all start from an empty void.

buildup.text: The Greek 'Chaos' was a yawning gap—not disorder, but absence. Norse myth begins with Ginnungagap—the great void.

discovery.text: In Buddhist philosophy, shunyata—emptiness—is not absence but potential. The void is pregnant with possibility.

twist.text: Modern physics agrees: the quantum vacuum isn't empty. Virtual particles pop in and out. Nothing is something.

climax.text: The void is zero made mythic. Every creation story says the same thing: something came from nothing.

quiz.question: What does 'shunyata' mean in Buddhist philosophy?
